conventions: Shared-head coordination (e.g. 'calcium and vitamin D metabolism') is ONE span. Test: delete the other conjunct - if what remains is not a pathway name on its own, do not split.
A list of distinct heads (e.g. 'glycolysis and the pentose phosphate pathway') must be split into one span per item.
If a coordination is only partly marked (a conjunct left un-marked), the narrow span stays a TP and the full string is recorded as an FN - that FN carries the correct boundary.
A trailing 'pathway'/'pathways' may stay inside the span; a trailing 'metabolites'/'intermediates'/'genes'/'disorders' changes the referent and must be excluded.
When a disease phrase embeds a nameable pathway, span the pathway part ('urea cycle disorder' -> 'urea cycle').
